display: Category buyer for airport retail in Singapore. I'm looking for real hawker names that can be turned into gifts a traveller can carry. I also run half marathons and collect Peranakan tiles.

signals.text: Travellers keep asking our floor staff for gifts 'from a hawker', and the shelves still show the same three biscuit brands.
I'm looking for food gifts with a recognisable hawker or heritage name that already come in a shelf-stable retail format.
Brands with a name often have no giftable format, and makers with a format have no name. I keep hitting this gap and haven't found anyone who closes it.
I'm training for the December half marathon in Sentosa and doing long runs of 18–20 km on weekends.
I have 31 Peranakan tiles in a box and no wall to put them on.
The heritage wall has 6 slots, 2 are filled and 4 are open. The range review is mid-December, and the mid-review slides are due on 21 October.
I'm interested in sauces and pastes from known stalls (chilli crab, bak chor mee, laksa) if they can be made to last 12 months in a bag.
I'm rebuilding my supplier scorecard so small suppliers aren't penalised for lacking a QA department. I'm stuck on how to weigh packaging damage in transit.
Good small makers keep failing on shelf life. One I met was making to order in a home kitchen with an eight-week life, and I had to say no.
The director keeps asking why the heritage wall only has two products, and the rule sheet leaves little room.
I'm travelling to Johor most weekends, so my free time is tight.

offers.text: Fifteen years of retail buying, six in food gifting, covering about 140 SKUs across four airport shops. I can give frank feedback on whether a product suits airport retail.
A supplier onboarding checklist I wrote myself, covering shelf life, labelling, halal pathway, minimum order and retail margin. I can walk a small maker through it.
A scorecard approach that accepts a third-party lab report in place of in-house QA, which helps small suppliers get through.
Contacts at two logistics firms that handle ambient and chilled air freight from Changi, including consolidated ambient pallets from Johor twice a week.
A weekly sell-through view by brand and month, so I can tell a maker what actually sells in airport gifting without sharing internal tables.
Tasting sessions at the Terminal 2 back office. I give structured feedback on taste, packaging, price and shelf life.
A sample drawer of rejected products, which I can use to show what usually fails (shelf life, labelling, leakage).
I can pace a running partner at 6:40/km on weekend long runs at East Coast Park.
I know Peranakan tiles and the Joo Chiat flea market, and I'm happy to talk heritage design.

catchers.hypo: I'm a manufacturer with a co-packing line and a 12-month shelf-stable pouch format. I'm looking for a known hawker name to partner with and make a product together.
catchers.can: I can introduce the idea to my heritage range as a candidate for one of the open slots. I can also share the onboarding checklist and the halal-pathway requirements.
catchers.confirm: Is your product ambient and shelf-stable for at least 12 months, made under your own name or the hawker's, rather than as a white-label from an anonymous lab?

catchers.hypo: I run a well-known hawker stall. Customers often ask for something to take home, but I have no packaging or food safety setup.
catchers.can: I can explain what a stall needs to become a giftable product, and suggest co-packers or labs who can help turn the recipe into a format. I can't promise a shelf slot.
catchers.confirm: Would you be willing to partner with a manufacturer to turn your recipe into an ambient, 12-month shelf-stable product?

catchers.hypo: I'm a food scientist or lab. I can extend shelf life for small makers and issue test reports. How do I get the report accepted by retailers?
catchers.can: I can show how my scorecard treats a lab report in place of in-house QA, and tell you which fields buyers actually look at.
catchers.confirm: Do your reports cover shelf life, labelling and packaging in transit, rather than just a safety test?

catchers.hypo: I run a family food business in or near Johor. I produce ambient goods and want a route into Singapore retail.
catchers.can: I can put you in touch with my logistics contact for consolidated ambient pallets from Johor, and I can visit your site in person on one of my Johor weekends.
catchers.confirm: Are your products entirely ambient, with no chilled or frozen items, and can they be exported with halal certification or a clear pathway to it?

catchers.hypo: I work on halal certification or food labelling for small brands. Do you know anyone who needs help planning a certification pathway?
catchers.can: I can introduce your service to makers who need a halal pathway for the heritage range, and share which questions retail buyers ask first.
catchers.confirm: Do you work with small food producers on first-time certification and labelling, rather than only large manufacturers?

catchers.hypo: I'm a packaging designer. I want to make a heritage food gift that survives travel without leaking or breaking.
catchers.can: I can give a buyer's view of what damages gifts in transit and gate sales, and suggest where you could test a prototype with my team.
catchers.confirm: Have you designed packaging for food that must survive a long bag journey, such as sauces, rather than only boxes for display?

catchers.hypo: I'm a merchandiser or retail designer. I want to create a story wall that a stranger can understand in ten seconds at a gate.
catchers.can: I can connect you with Priya, my merchandising colleague, who knows what the director actually thinks and how walls are signed off.
catchers.confirm: Have you designed a physical retail display for a travel or airport environment, rather than only online or standard supermarkets?

catchers.hypo: I'm a half-marathon runner in Singapore looking for a long-run partner at a slow pace this season.
catchers.can: I can join you on a weekend long run at East Coast Park. I'm training for the Sentosa half in December.
catchers.confirm: Are you comfortable running about 6:40/km on 16–20 km runs early on weekend mornings?

catchers.hypo: I sell old Peranakan tiles or run a heritage craft stall, and I'm looking for people who appreciate chipped, honest pieces.
catchers.can: I can talk about tiles and Joo Chiat, and consider a purchase. I don't have wall space.
catchers.confirm: Are you selling genuine vintage Peranakan tiles at flea-market prices, rather than modern reproductions?

forbids.text: I can't list chilled or frozen products. I'm limited to ambient freight.
Nothing goes on the heritage wall unless it is shelf-stable for 12 months and has a clear halal pathway.
I don't take white-label or lab-only products with no recognisable name behind them.
I don't take a single hawker without a product format.
I can't promise a listing. Wall decisions go through my director and the range review.
Weekends are mostly taken by travel, so I don't take weekend meetings.

projects.name: Heritage food gifting range ('Taste of Singapore' wall)
projects.text: I'm filling the 4 open slots on a wall of 6 near the main gates. Products need a recognisable heritage name, 12 months of shelf stability and a halal pathway. The range review is mid-December.
roles_needed: heritage food brand or hawker with a name
co-packer or manufacturer with a shelf-stable format
food scientist or lab for shelf-life reports

projects.name: Supplier scorecard v3
projects.text: A scorecard that doesn't penalise small suppliers for lacking QA. It accepts a lab report in lieu of in-house QA, and I still need a way to weigh packaging damage in transit.

policy.t1: When there's a real lead, I can share the heritage wall rules, open slots, review dates, and rough order-size and margin ranges.
policy.t2: Once trust is established I can share what has failed so far, the pressure on the project, and the general fact that I travel to see family in Johor.
policy.never: Mum's medical details, my salary and bonus, internal margin tables, and my private feelings about my job.
